haiku-low.q1: It returns 202 only after the raw log confirms the write of accepted events. The response lists rejected events by batch position and reason.
haiku-low.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off from 1 second up to 5 minutes. It never resends rejected events.
haiku-low.q3: The copy with the lowest raw log offset wins. Dedup keys expire after 8 days, so a late copy may load live; replay keeps the lowest offset.
haiku-low.q4: Tuesday. Day is the UTC date of server-stamped received_at, so it belongs to Tuesday's partition and Tuesday's replay.
haiku-low.q5: In the existing key-value store, keyed by event_id. Each key expires after 8 days via TTL.
haiku-low.q6: Collector still accepts them into the raw log. Live processor stops before loading, does not commit; events wait up to 14 days; lag alert fires.
haiku-low.q7: It does not fully avoid double-counting: a crash after load can load events twice. Whether warehouse load can merge on event_id is an open question.
haiku-low.q8: It reads archive entries with received_at from 8 days before D through end of D. Rebuilt events are written to a staging table, then atomically swapped into partition D.
haiku-low.q9: It keeps the lowest-offset copy of each event_id, only if its received_at is on D. Reading archive from D-8 covers earlier first copies.
haiku-low.q10: If it fails before the swap, events_clean is unchanged; rerun it. The swap is atomic. Failure during the swap is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q11: Only closed days that live processing has finished. Fixes are possible until about 82 days after the day ends.

sonnet.q1: It rejects each malformed event individually (missing event_id or device_id, or over 32 KB) to the reject bucket, writes the rest to the raw log, and returns 202 only after the raw log confirms the write. The 202 lists rejected events by batch position and reason.
sonnet.q2: It resends the same batch with the same event_ids, backing off from 1 second up to 5 minutes. Unacknowledged events stay in an on-device buffer for up to 7 days. It never resends rejected events.
sonnet.q3: The first copy (lowest raw log offset) wins; later copies are dropped. Live: dropped if event_id is in the dedup store (8-day TTL) or earlier in the same batch. Replay keeps the lowest-offset copy, only if its received_at is on D. Copies arriving after the 8-day window are not covered by the dedup store; only replay's 8-day lookback is described, so the exact outcome for copies more than 8 days apart is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q4: Day is the UTC date of received_at (server time), so it belongs to Tuesday's partition and Tuesday's replay. The client timestamp is not used.
sonnet.q5: In the dedup store (existing key-value store). The key is event_id, recorded for each loaded event (written once per batch after the load). Each key expires after 8 days (TTL).
sonnet.q6: The collector still accepts and writes them to the raw log (it does no dedup). The live processor stops before loading and does not commit; events wait in the raw log for up to 14 days and the lag alert fires.
sonnet.q7: NOT STATED as solved. The document says events may load twice in this case (open question: it needs the warehouse load to merge on event_id, undecided). Not losing: the offset is not committed, so the batch is reprocessed. Replay of the day can later fix duplicates.
sonnet.q8: It reads archive entries with received_at from 8 days before D through the end of D. Results are written to a staging table, then atomically swapped in for partition D of events_clean.
sonnet.q9: It doesn't use the dedup store. It reads the archive from D-8 through end of D, and for each event_id keeps the copy with the lowest raw log offset, keeping it only if its received_at is on D. So if the first copy was on an earlier day, the event is not in D's output.
sonnet.q10: If it fails before the swap, events_clean is unchanged (the swap is atomic, so dashboards see old or new, never a mix). The operator reruns it.
sonnet.q11: Only closed days (next day has reached 02:00 UTC) that the live processor has finished (committed offset at or past the first raw log entry after 02:00 UTC on the day after D). Also limited by archive retention: about 82 days after the day ends.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. It is an open question: drop or keep with a flag; product has not decided.
